answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks from independently anchored identities, limiting how far unverified endorsements can spread. A Sybil cluster—even one styled “nebula” or “ivory”—often forms an island connected to honest nodes by a sparse external cut. Its low conductance constrains walk escape and, under capped seed weight and bounded propagation, limits the cluster’s aggregate voting influence; min-cut bounds make that constraint explicit.
